cohort: Women who underwent caesarean section at a secondary hospital in regional New Zealand
finding: The use of hydrocolloid dressings after caesarean section showed promising results with regard to SSI rates and cost reduction, but this needs to be balanced with potentially reduced midwifery and nursing satisfaction due to difficulty removing the dressings.
mod_finding: This study investigated the use of hydrocolloid dressings compared to basic contact dressings for cesarean sections, focusing on surgical site infection rates and cost.
